description: An operator's number of scans is how many scan records they have.

b.request: For each `scans.crewref`, count its scan records and average `gbsize / spanmin` over scans with nonmissing values; select operators whose average exceeds the unweighted average of those operator averages, then return one row with the unrounded average scan-record count, average GB per minute, and average excess over the all-operator average
b.sql: WITH operator_stats AS (SELECT crewref, COUNT(*) AS scan_record_count, AVG(gbsize / NULLIF(spanmin, 0)) AS avg_gb_per_minute FROM scans GROUP BY crewref), overall AS (SELECT AVG(avg_gb_per_minute) AS all_operator_avg FROM operator_stats) SELECT AVG(o.scan_record_count) AS avg_scan_record_count, AVG(o.avg_gb_per_minute) AS avg_gb_per_minute, AVG(o.avg_gb_per_minute - a.all_operator_avg) AS avg_excess_gb_per_minute FROM operator_stats o CROSS JOIN overall a WHERE o.avg_gb_per_minute > a.all_operator_avg

a.request: For each operator (`scans.crewref`), find their number of scans by counting their scan records, and find their average file size per minute, computed per scan as `gbsize` ÷ `spanmin`. Ignore missing values. Consider only operators whose average GB per minute is above the simple average of that figure across all operators. In a single row, give the average number of scans of those operators, their average GB per minute, and their average margin above the all-operator average, with no rounding.
a.sql: WITH operator_stats AS (SELECT crewref, COUNT(*) AS scan_count, AVG(gbsize / NULLIF(spanmin, 0)) AS avg_gb_per_minute FROM scans GROUP BY crewref), overall AS (SELECT AVG(avg_gb_per_minute) AS all_operator_avg FROM operator_stats) SELECT AVG(o.scan_count) AS avg_scan_count, AVG(o.avg_gb_per_minute) AS avg_gb_per_minute, AVG(o.avg_gb_per_minute - a.all_operator_avg) AS avg_margin_above_all_operators FROM operator_stats o CROSS JOIN overall a WHERE o.avg_gb_per_minute > a.all_operator_avg;

c.request: Look at the operators (`scans.crewref`) whose average file size per minute, computed per scan as `gbsize` ÷ `spanmin` with missing values ignored, is above the simple average of that figure across all operators. In a single row, how many scans have these operators done on average, what is their average GB per minute, and by how much on average do they exceed the all-operator figure? Don't round. An operator's number of scans is how many scan records they have.
c.sql: WITH operator_stats AS (SELECT crewref, COUNT(*) AS scan_count, AVG(gbsize / NULLIF(spanmin, 0)) AS avg_gb_per_minute FROM scans GROUP BY crewref), overall AS (SELECT AVG(avg_gb_per_minute) AS all_operator_avg FROM operator_stats) SELECT AVG(o.scan_count) AS avg_scan_count, AVG(o.avg_gb_per_minute) AS avg_gb_per_minute, AVG(o.avg_gb_per_minute - a.all_operator_avg) AS avg_excess_gb_per_minute FROM operator_stats AS o CROSS JOIN overall AS a WHERE o.avg_gb_per_minute > a.all_operator_avg;

d.request: For operators identified by `scans.crewref`, compute each operator’s average GB per minute from per-scan `gbsize` ÷ `spanmin`, ignoring missing values. Select operators whose average exceeds the simple average of this figure across all operators. In a single row, report their average number of scans (counting scan records per operator), their average GB per minute, and the average amount by which they exceed the all-operator figure. Do not round.
d.sql: WITH operator_stats AS (SELECT crewref, COUNT(*) AS scan_count, AVG(gbsize / NULLIF(spanmin, 0)) AS avg_gb_per_minute FROM scans GROUP BY crewref), overall AS (SELECT AVG(avg_gb_per_minute) AS avg_gb_per_minute FROM operator_stats) SELECT AVG(o.scan_count) AS avg_scan_count, AVG(o.avg_gb_per_minute) AS avg_gb_per_minute, AVG(o.avg_gb_per_minute - a.avg_gb_per_minute) AS avg_excess_gb_per_minute FROM operator_stats o CROSS JOIN overall a WHERE o.avg_gb_per_minute > a.avg_gb_per_minute;
